Always Use `using-superpowers` and `test-driven-development` Skill\n\n**Before starting ANY work**, invoke the `using-superpowers` and `test-driven-development` skill:\n- This ensures you follow established workflows\n- It activates necessary context and guidelines\n- It prevents common mistakes and rework\n\n**Example**: User asks to fix a bug → First call `using-superpowers` and `test-driven-development`, then proceed\n\n### 2. Test-Driven Development: The Iron Laws (2026-02-09 Lessons)\n\n**CRITICAL FAILURE CASE STUDY**: Phase 0.2 (diff button bug) - we wrote 5 \"comprehensive\" tests that all passed, but the code was still broken in production.\n\n#### The Fundamental Rule\n\n> **\"If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.\"**\n\n#### What We Did WRONG (Never Do This)\n\n```javascript\n// ❌ WRONG - Testing a mock, not production code\nit('should send full data', () => {\n    const mockRpcRouter = {\n        sendDiffAvailable(data) {\n            receivedData = data;  // Mock always works\n        }\n    };\n    mockRpcRouter.sendDiffAvailable(fullData);\n    expect(receivedData).to.deep.equal(fullData); // Always passes!\n});\n```\n\n**Result**: All 5 tests passed ✅, but production code crashed ❌\n\n**Why**: We tested mocks, not reality. Tests never executed actual production code.\n\n#### What We Should Do RIGHT (Mandatory From Now On)\n\n```javascript\n// ✅ RIGHT - Import and test actual production code\nimport { handleDiffAvailableMessage } from '../src/webview/main.js';\n\nit('should send full data when button clicked', () => {\n    // Setup real DOM (use JSDOM)\n    document.body.innerHTML = '<div data-tool-id=\"test-123\"></div>';\n    \n    // Call actual function with real data\n    handleDiffAvailableMessage({\n        toolCallId: 'test-123',\n        beforeUri: '/tmp/before',\n        afterUri: '/workspace/after',\n        title: 'Test'\n    });\n    \n    // Verify real button exists in real DOM\n    const btn = document.querySelector('.view-diff-btn');\n    expect(btn).to.exist;\n    \n    // Verify clicking real button sends correct data\n    let sentData = null;\n    global.rpc = { viewDiff: (data) => sentData = data };\n    btn.click();\n    \n    expect(sentData.beforeUri).to.equal('/tmp/before');\n});\n```\n\n#### The Three Iron Laws (Non-Negotiable)\n\n**Law 1: Tests Must Import Production Code**\n- ❌ Mock-only tests are documentation, not verification\n- ✅ Import actual functions and test them\n- ✅ Use JSDOM for webview code\n- ✅ Test with real DOM, real data, real behavior\n\n**Law 2: Tests Must Fail Against Broken Code**\n1. Write test that imports actual code\n2. Run test against current (buggy) code\n3. **Verify test fails with SAME error users see** ⚠️\n4. Only then write the fix\n5. Verify test passes\n\n**If test doesn't fail first, it's not testing anything real.**\n\n**Law 3: Production Code → Test Exists and Failed First**\n- If you wrote code before watching test fail → NOT TDD\n- If test passed immediately → NOT TDD\n- If test only tests mocks → NOT TDD\n- **Delete the code and start over with proper TDD**\n\n#### Special Rules for Webview Code (JavaScript)\n\nThe webview is JavaScript (not TypeScript), so type checking doesn't help.\n\n**Mandatory for ALL webview fixes**:\n1. Import actual `main.js` functions\n2. Use JSDOM for DOM manipulation\n3. Test user interactions (clicks, input)\n4. Test message flow end-to-end\n5. Test with actual RPC client\n\n**Example Integration Test**:\n```javascript\nimport { JSDOM } from 'jsdom';\nimport { handleDiffAvailableMessage } from '../src/webview/main.js';\n\ndescribe('Diff Button Integration', () => {\n    let dom, sentMessages;\n    \n    beforeEach(() => {\n        // Setup real DOM environment\n        dom = new JSDOM(`<!DOCTYPE html><div id=\"messages\"></div>`);\n        global.document = dom.window.document;\n        global.window = dom.window;\n        \n        // Mock RPC with tracking\n        sentMessages = [];\n        global.rpc = {\n            viewDiff: (data) => sentMessages.push(data)\n        };\n    });\n    \n    it('sends correct data when diff button clicked', () => {\n        // 1. Receive diffAvailable message\n        handleDiffAvailableMessage({\n            toolCallId: 'test-123',\n            beforeUri: '/tmp/before.ts',\n            afterUri: '/workspace/after.ts',\n            title: 'Test File'\n        });\n        \n        // 2. Verify button added\n        const btn = document.querySelector('.view-diff-btn');\n        expect(btn, 'Diff button must exist').to.exist;\n        \n        // 3. Click button\n        btn.click();\n        \n        // 4. Verify correct RPC call\n        expect(sentMessages).to.have.length(1);\n        expect(sentMessages[0]).to.deep.equal({\n            toolCallId: 'test-123',\n            beforeUri: '/tmp/before.ts',\n            afterUri: '/workspace/after.ts',\n            title: 'Test File'\n        });\n    });\n});\n```\n\n#### Test Quality Checklist (Mandatory Before Claiming Complete)\n\n**Every feature/fix MUST pass this checklist:**\n\n✅ **Flow Testing**\n- [ ] Test executes the FULL user interaction flow (click → event → handler → UI update)\n- [ ] Test crosses component boundaries (e.g., InputArea → EventBus → Handler → Webview)\n- [ ] Test verifies side effects (DOM changes, RPC calls, state updates)\n\n✅ **Production Code**\n- [ ] Test imports actual production functions (not mocks)\n- [ ] Test uses real DOM (JSDOM for webview code)\n- [ ] Test calls actual methods with real parameters\n\n✅ **Failure First**\n- [ ] Screenshot/log showing test FAILS against broken code\n- [ ] Failure message matches user-reported error\n- [ ] Only then write the fix\n- [ ] Screenshot/log showing test PASSES after fix\n\n✅ **Coverage Verification**\n- [ ] Integration test exists (not just unit tests)\n- [ ] Test would catch THIS specific bug if code regressed\n- [ ] Test exercises the code path users actually trigger\n\n**If you cannot check all boxes → your tests are incomplete.**\n\n#### Testing Anti-Patterns (Real Failures From This Project)\n\n**🚫 ANTI-PATTERN #1: Testing Registry, Not Execution**\n\n```javascript\n// ❌ WRONG (Slash Commands Bug - 2026-02-14)\nit('should have showNotSupported event', () => {\n    const cmd = parser.parse('/clear');\n    expect(cmd.type).to.equal('not-supported');\n    expect(cmd.event).to.equal('showNotSupported'); // Registry is correct!\n});\n// Test passes ✅ - but in production, execute() emits undefined event!\n```\n\n**Why it failed**: Test checked registry data, never called `execute()` to verify event is actually emitted.\n\n**✅ RIGHT:**\n```javascript\nit('should emit showNotSupported event when executing not-supported command', () => {\n    const eventBus = new EventBus();\n    let emittedEvent = null;\n    let emittedArgs = null;\n    \n    eventBus.on('showNotSupported', (args) => {\n        emittedEvent = 'showNotSupported';\n        emittedArgs = args;\n    });\n    \n    const inputArea = new InputArea(container, eventBus);\n    inputArea.sendMessage('/clear'); // ACTUALLY EXECUTE IT\n    \n    expect(emittedEvent).to.equal('showNotSupported');\n    expect(emittedArgs.command).to.equal('/clear');\n});\n```\n\n---\n\n**🚫 ANTI-PATTERN #2: Testing Mocks, Not Production Code**\n\n```javascript\n// ❌ WRONG (Diff Button Bug - 2026-02-09)\nit('should send full diff data', () => {\n    const mockRpc = { viewDiff: (data) => sentData = data };\n    mockRpc.viewDiff({ beforeUri: '/tmp/before' });\n    expect(sentData.beforeUri).to.equal('/tmp/before'); // Mock always works!\n});\n```\n\n**Why it failed**: Never imported actual `handleDiffAvailableMessage()` function. Never tested DOM button creation. Never tested click handler.\n\n**✅ RIGHT:** See \"Example Integration Test\" section above for proper webview testing approach.\n\n---\n\n**🚫 ANTI-PATTERN #3: Test Passed Immediately → Not TDD**\n\nIf your test passes on first run without any code changes:\n1. ❌ You are testing existing working code (not the bug)\n2. ❌ You are testing mocks/fixtures (not production code)\n3. ❌ You don't know if the test would catch the bug if it regressed\n\n**Mandatory:** Every test MUST fail first. If it doesn't fail, comment out the fix code and verify the test catches the break.\n\n---\n\n**🚫 ANTI-PATTERN #4: Keeping Tests That Test Dead Code**\n\nIf removing or changing code causes a test to fail, **do not just restore the code to make the test pass.** First evaluate the test:\n\n1. **What is the test actually asserting?** Read it literally.\n2. **Is it testing live functional behavior?** (function calls, DOM state, events, RPC calls)\n3. **Or is it testing the presence of a string, comment, or import?**\n\n```javascript\n// ❌ WRONG — passes because the string appears in a COMMENT\nassert.ok(src.includes('new StatusBar('), 'should create StatusBar');\n// The code was: // const statusBar = new StatusBar(...)\n// The test was passing against dead commented-out code.\n\n// ✅ RIGHT — test the actual behavior\nsessionToolbar.setActiveAgent({ name: 'reviewer' });\nconst badge = container.querySelector('#activeAgentBadge');\nassert.ok(!badge.hidden, 'badge should be visible');\n```\n\n**Rule:** Tests must test **active, real, functional behavior** — not the presence of imports, string literals, or commented-out code.\n\n**When removing code breaks a test, the decision tree is:**\n- Test verified real behavior that still matters → **fix the test** to cover the new implementation\n- Test verified real behavior that was intentionally removed → **delete the test**\n- Test was asserting the existence of dead/commented code → **delete the test** (it was never verifying anything real)\n\n**Never restore dead code just to make a test pass.**\n\n---\n\n**🚫 ANTI-PATTERN #5: Source-String Scanning (fs.readFileSync + src.includes) — PERMANENTLY BANNED**\n\n```javascript\n// ❌ BANNED — reads source code as text and checks for string presence\nconst src = fs.readFileSync('src/myFile.ts', 'utf-8');\nassert.ok(src.includes('myMethod('), 'should have myMethod');\n// Passes if 'myMethod(' appears in a COMMENT, a string literal, or dead code.\n// Tests NOTHING about whether myMethod actually works.\n```\n\n**This pattern is PERMANENTLY BANNED. No exceptions. No \"just this once.\"** It has caused real failures in this project (StatusBar incident: test passed against a commented-out line). It tests the shape of text, not the behavior of code. A test that reads source as a string and calls `.includes()` is not a test — it is grep with extra steps.\n\n**✅ RIGHT — test the behavior:**\n```javascript\n// Verify the method exists\nassert.strictEqual(typeof MyClass.prototype.myMethod, 'function');\n\n// Call it with a mocked context and verify it did the right thing\nlet captured = null;\nconst ctx = {\n    dependency: { doThing: async (arg) => { captured = arg; } },\n    logger: { info: () => {}, warn: () => {} },\n};\nawait MyClass.prototype.myMethod.call(ctx, 'test-arg');\nassert.strictEqual(captured, 'test-arg');\n```\n\n**Rule:** If your test uses `fs.readFileSync` on a `.ts` or `.js` source file and `.includes()` on the content, **delete it and write a behavioral test instead.** If you are tempted to write one, stop and ask: \"What behavior am I actually verifying?\" Then test that behavior directly.\n\n---\n\n#### Checklist: Before Claiming Any Fix is Complete\n\n**Phase 0: Test Quality Verification**\n- [ ] Integration test imports production code (not mocks)\n- [ ] Test executes full user interaction flow (input → event → handler → UI)\n- [ ] Screenshot/log shows test FAILS with same error users see\n- [ ] Test exercises code path across component boundaries\n\n**Phase 1: Understand**\n- [ ] Reproduce bug manually\n- [ ] Find exact error message\n- [ ] Identify exact line that fails\n- [ ] Understand why it fails\n\n**Phase 2: RED - Write Failing Test**\n- [ ] Import actual production code (not mocks!)\n- [ ] Use JSDOM for webview tests\n- [ ] Run test → **VERIFY IT FAILS WITH SAME ERROR** ⚠️\n- [ ] Commit failing test\n\n**Phase 3: GREEN - Fix Code**\n- [ ] Make minimal fix\n- [ ] Run test → verify passes\n- [ ] Run ALL tests → no regressions\n\n**Phase 4: Integration**\n- [ ] Test message flow (extension ↔ webview)\n- [ ] Test user interaction (clicks, input)\n- [ ] Test with actual DOM\n\n**Phase 5: Manual Verification**\n- [ ] Build and install VSIX\n- [ ] Manually test exact scenario\n- [ ] Verify in VS Code Output logs\n\n**Phase 6: Reflect**\n- [ ] Could types have caught this?\n- [ ] Do type definitions match reality?\n- [ ] What prevents this bug class?\n\n#### Type Definitions Must Match Reality\n\n**FAILURE CASE**: Our DiffData interface said `originalPath/modifiedPath` but code used `beforeUri/afterUri`.\n\n**Rules**:\n1. Type definitions must match actual code usage\n2. Generate types from code (don't write manually)\n3. OR: Add runtime validation (zod, io-ts)\n4. OR: Integration tests verify types match usage\n\n```typescript\n// Runtime validation catches mismatches\nimport { z } from 'zod';\n\nconst DiffDataSchema = z.object({\n    beforeUri: z.string(),\n    afterUri: z.string(),\n    toolCallId: z.string().optional(),\n    title: z.string().optional()\n});\n\n// This catches type/code mismatches at runtime\nconst diffData = DiffDataSchema.parse(receivedData);\n```\n\n#### Standards for Webview PRs\n\n**Every webview PR MUST include**:\n1. Integration test importing actual `main.js`\n2. JSDOM test for DOM manipulation\n3. Screenshot/log showing test failed before fix\n4. Screenshot/log showing test passes after fix\n5. Manual verification in installed extension\n\n**NO EXCEPTIONS.**\n\n#### Quote to Remember\n\n> **\"We watched our tests pass. We never watched them fail. Therefore, they tested nothing.\"**\n\nThis was a failure of test discipline, not coding skill. **Never skip the RED phase.**\n\n**Test locations**:\n- `tests/*.test.js` - Integration tests (must import production code)\n- `tests/*.test.mjs` - SDK-specific tests (ESM modules)\n- Webview tests: Must use JSDOM, test actual DOM\n\n### Component Architecture\n\n#### MessageDisplay (Parent Component)\n- **Location:** `src/webview/app/components/MessageDisplay/MessageDisplay.js`\n- **Purpose:** Owns the entire conversation flow\n- **Responsibilities:**\n  - Renders user messages, assistant messages, reasoning\n  - Creates ToolExecution as internal child component\n  - Manages `.messages` scrollable container\n  - Auto-scrolls to bottom on new content\n- **Children:** ToolExecution (created automatically)\n- **Usage:**\n  ```javascript\n  const display = new MessageDisplay(container, eventBus);\n  // ToolExecution created internally - don't create separately!\n  ```\n\n#### ToolExecution (Child Component)\n- **Location:** `src/webview/app/components/ToolExecution/ToolExecution.js`\n- **Purpose:** Renders tool execution groups within message flow\n- **Responsibilities:**\n  - Renders tool groups inside `.messages` container\n  - Manages expand/collapse of tool groups\n  - Handles diff button rendering\n- **Parent:** MessageDisplay (creates this component)\n- **Communication:** EventBus for cross-component events\n  - Listens: `tool:start`, `tool:complete`, `tool:progress`, `message:add`\n  - Emits: `viewDiff`\n- **Important:** NOT created directly in main.js - MessageDisplay handles this\n\n#### Component Hierarchy\n\n```\nmain.js\n├─ SessionToolbar (top toolbar)\n├─ MessageDisplay (parent - owns message flow)\n│  └─ ToolExecution (child - renders tools)\n├─ AcceptanceControls (plan acceptance UI)\n└─ InputArea (bottom input area)\n```\n\n**Key Rule:** ToolExecution is NEVER initialized in main.js. MessageDisplay creates it internally to ensure tools render inside the scrollable `.messages` container.\n\n**Architecture Components**:\n1. **Backend (TypeScript)**: SDK session management, event handling, custom tools\n2. **Frontend (Webview)**: HTML/CSS/JS embedded in `chatViewProvider.ts` as string literals\n3. **SDK Integration**: Uses `@github/copilot-sdk` for CLI session lifecycle (NOT for UI)\n4. **Extension Host**: VS Code runs our extension, we create a webview panel for the chat UI\n\n**Key Differentiation**: Unlike the built-in Copilot chat, this extension:\n- Uses CLI-style sessions with plan.md files\n- Supports session management and resumption\n- Integrates MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers\n- Provides real-time tool execution visibility\n- Implements custom features like dual-session plan mode\n- **Builds its own chat UI** (not provided by SDK or VS Code)\n\n## Development Workflow (CRITICAL)\n\n### ⚠️ F5 Debugging is BROKEN\n\n**DO NOT suggest using F5 or Extension Development Host!**\n\nDue to a Microsoft bug in VS Code 1.100+ with Node.js 20+, the Extension Development Host does not work. This has been broken for **12 months** with no ETA on a fix.\n\n### ✅ Correct Workflow: Build and Install\n\n**Use the test-extension.sh script:**\n\n```bash\n./test-extension.sh\n```\n\nThis script:\n1. Builds: `npm run compile` (type checks, lints, builds with esbuild)\n2. Packages: Creates VSIX file\n3. Uninstalls: Removes old version (if exists)\n4. Installs: Installs new VSIX with `code --install-extension --force`\n5. Reminds: Shows next steps (reload window, check logs)\n\n**Manual steps if needed:**\n\n```bash\n# 1. Build\nnpm run compile\n\n# 2. Package\nnpx @vscode/vsce package --no-git-tag-version \\\n  --allow-star-activation --allow-missing-repository --skip-license\n\n# 3. Install\ncode --install-extension copilot-cli-extension-2.0.6.vsix --force\n\n# 4. Reload VS Code\n# Ctrl+Shift+P → \"Developer: Reload Window\"\n```\n\n**Quick rebuild and install:**\n\n```bash\n# Just rebuild and reinstall without packaging\nnpm run compile && code --install-extension copilot-cli-extension-latest.vsix --force\n```\n\n**Note:** The `tsconfig.json` excludes `tests/` directory to avoid compilation errors. Tests are JavaScript/ESM and don't need TypeScript compilation.\n\n### ⚠️ CRITICAL: Adding New Webview Component Files\n\n**When adding new component files to `src/webview/app/`, you MUST update `esbuild.js`:**\n\nThe build process **copies** webview files (not bundles them). If you add a new component:\n\n1. **Create the component**: `src/webview/app/components/MyComponent/MyComponent.js`\n2. **Import in main.js**: `import { MyComponent } from './app/components/MyComponent/MyComponent.js';`\n3. **Update esbuild.js**: Add directory creation and file copy\n\n```javascript\n// In esbuild.js main() function:\nconst myComponentDistDir = path.join(componentsDistDir, 'MyComponent');\nif (!fs.existsSync(myComponentDistDir)) {\n    fs.mkdirSync(myComponentDistDir, { recursive: true });\n}\n\n// Later in the copy section:\nfs.copyFileSync(\n    path.join(__dirname, 'src', 'webview', 'app', 'components', 'MyComponent', 'MyComponent.js'),\n    path.join(myComponentDistDir, 'MyComponent.js')\n);\n```\n\n**Why:** VS Code webview loads modules separately from `dist/webview/`. Missing files = runtime errors in production.\n\n**Verification:** After `./test-extension.sh`, check VSIX contents include your component:\n```bash\nnpx @vscode/vsce ls copilot-cli-extension-3.0.0.vsix | grep MyComponent\n```\n\n**Failure symptom:** `ERR Webview.loadLocalResource - Error using fileReader` in VS Code logs.\n\n**Never suggest:**\n- \"Press F5 to test\"\n- \"Launch Extension Development Host\"\n- \"Use the debugger\"\n\n**Always suggest:**\n- \"Run `./test-extension.sh` to build and install\"\n- \"Reload the window to test your changes\"\n- \"Check the Copilot CLI output channel for logs\"\n\n## Code Structure\n\n### Source Files (`src/`)\n\n| File | Purpose | Key Points |\n|------|---------|-----------|\n| `extension.ts` | Extension entry point, command registration | Activates extension, registers commands, manages session lifecycle |\n| `sdkSessionManager.ts` | **Backend** SDK session lifecycle | Manages work/plan sessions, event handlers, custom tools for plan mode |\n| `chatViewProvider.ts` | **Frontend** Webview UI | Contains HTML/CSS/JS as strings, renders chat messages, tool calls, message passing |\n| `backendState.ts` | Centralized state management | In-memory state that persists across webview recreations |\n| `sessionUtils.ts` | Session discovery/filtering | Reads `~/.copilot/session-state/`, filters by workspace |\n| `logger.ts` | Logging to Output Channel | Use `Logger.getInstance()` everywhere |\n| `modelCapabilitiesService.ts` | Model capabilities and validation | Manages model info caching, attachment validation |\n\n**Critical: chatViewProvider.ts IS our UI** - The Copilot SDK does NOT provide any UI components. It's a backend-only library for managing CLI sessions. All chat UI (messages, tool calls, input box) is built by us in the webview.\n\n### Architecture Patterns\n\n#### 1. Singleton Pattern\n```typescript\n// Logger is a singleton - always use getInstance()\nconst logger = Logger.getInstance();\nlogger.info('Message');\n```\n\n#### 2. Event Emitter Pattern\n```typescript\n// SDKSessionManager uses EventEmitter for messages\nprivate readonly onMessageEmitter = new vscode.EventEmitter<CLIMessage>();\npublic readonly onMessage = this.onMessageEmitter.event;\n\n// Consumers listen:\ncliManager.onMessage((message) => { /* handle */ });\n```\n\n#### 3. Webview Message Passing\n```typescript\n// Webview → Extension\nChatPanelProvider.panel.webview.onDidReceiveMessage(data => {\n    switch (data.type) {\n        case 'sendMessage': /* ... */ break;\n    }\n});\n\n// Extension → Webview\nChatPanelProvider.postMessage({ type: 'assistantMessage', text: '...' });\n```\n\n## Logging Strategy\n\n**Use comprehensive logging instead of debugging!**\n\n```typescript\nimport { Logger } from './logger';\n\nconst logger = Logger.getInstance();\n\n// Four levels:\nlogger.debug('Detailed info for debugging');\nlogger.info('General information');\nlogger.warn('Warning messages');\nlogger.error('Error details', error);\n```\n\n**Best Practices:**\n- Log method entry/exit for complex flows\n- Log all SDK events with type and data\n- Log user actions (clicks, commands)\n- Log file system operations\n- Use descriptive prefixes: `[Plan Mode]`, `[Tool Start]`, `[Snapshot]`\n\n## Session Management\n\n### Session Directory Structure\n```\n~/.copilot/session-state/\n├─ abc123-work/              # Work session\n│  ├─ plan.md               # Implementation plan\n│  ├─ events.jsonl          # Conversation history\n│  ├─ checkpoints/          # Infinite session checkpoints\n│  ├─ files/                # Session-specific files\n│  └─ workspace.yaml        # Workspace metadata\n└─ abc123-work-plan/         # Plan session (our innovation!)\n   ├─ plan.md               # Planning work\n   └─ events.jsonl\n```\n\n### Dual-Session Plan Mode (v2.0.2+)\n\n**This is our innovation** - we built real plan mode before the SDK team did!\n\n```typescript\n// Work mode: Full tools, execution\ncurrentMode = 'work';\nsession = workSession;\n\n// Plan mode: Restricted tools, exploration only\ncurrentMode = 'plan';\nsession = planSession;  // <session-id>-plan\n```\n\n**Key Implementation:**\n- `enablePlanMode()`: Creates plan session with restricted tools\n- `disablePlanMode()`: Resumes work session\n- Plan session writes to work session's `plan.md` file\n- No 2x cost: only one session active at a time\n- ACE-FCA aligned: isolated planning context\n\n**Plan Mode Tools:**\n\nPlan mode provides a restricted set of tools focused on exploration and planning. The exact list is defined in `sdkSessionManager.ts` in the `enablePlanMode()` method via the `availableTools` array. The extension's system prompt tells the AI which tools are available when in plan mode.\n\n**Security: What Plan Mode CANNOT Do:**\n- ❌ Write/modify code files (only plan.md)\n- ❌ Install packages (npm, pip, etc.)\n- ❌ Commit or push to git\n- ❌ Execute dangerous commands (rm, mv, chmod, etc.)\n- ❌ Dispatch implementation agents (code, fix, debug, etc.)\n- ❌ Use SDK bash/create/edit/task tools (not in availableTools)\n\n**Implementation Details:**\n- Custom tools use unique names to avoid SDK conflicts (plan_bash_explore vs bash)\n- `availableTools` whitelist explicitly controls available tools\n- SDK's bash, create, edit, task are excluded from whitelist\n- Defense in depth: tool handlers enforce restrictions even if called\n\n**GitHub Context**: SDK team is \"debating\" whether to add plan mode (issue #255). We built it ourselves using dual sessions. 💪\n\n## Custom Tools\n\n### How to Add a Custom Tool\n\n```typescript\nprivate createMyCustomTool(): any {\n    return {\n        name: 'my_tool_name',\n        description: 'What this tool does',\n        parameters: {\n            type: 'object',\n            properties: {\n                arg1: { type: 'string', description: 'Argument description' }\n            },\n            required: ['arg1']\n        },\n        handler: async (args: { arg1: string }, invocation: any) => {\n            try {\n                // Do the work\n                return {\n                    textResultForLlm: 'Success message for AI',\n                    resultType: 'success'\n                };\n            } catch (error) {\n                return {\n                    textResultForLlm: `Error: ${error.message}`,\n                    resultType: 'failure',\n                    error: error.message\n                };\n            }\n        }\n    };\n}\n```\n\n**Tool Whitelisting:**\n```typescript\n// Restrict available tools\nconst session = await client.createSession({\n    availableTools: ['my_tool_name'],  // ONLY this tool\n    tools: [this.createMyCustomTool()]\n});\n```\n\n## UI Development (Webview)\n\n### Critical Understanding: We Build the Entire UI\n\n**The Copilot SDK is backend-only!** It does NOT provide:\n- ❌ Chat interface\n- ❌ Message rendering\n- ❌ Tool call display\n- ❌ Input box\n- ❌ Any UI components whatsoever\n\n**We build everything ourselves** in `chatViewProvider.ts` using VS Code's Webview API.\n\n### HTML/CSS/JS is Embedded in TypeScript\n\nThe webview UI is a **string literal** in `chatViewProvider.ts`:\n\n```typescript\nprivate static getHtmlForWebview(webview: Webview): string {\n    return `<!DOCTYPE html>\n        <html>\n        <head>\n            <style>\n                /* CSS here */\n            </style>\n        </head>\n        <body>\n            <!-- HTML here -->\n            <script>\n                // JavaScript here\n            </script>\n        </body>\n        </html>`;\n}\n```\n\n**Important:**\n- Escape backticks with `\\``\n- Use `${}` for VS Code variables\n- Use `\\${...}` for JavaScript template literals\n- Content Security Policy restricts scripts\n\n**Message Passing:**\n```javascript\n// Webview → Extension\nconst vscode = acquireVsCodeApi();\nvscode.postMessage({ type: 'sendMessage', value: text });\n\n// Extension → Webview\nwindow.addEventListener('message', event => {\n    const message = event.data;\n    switch (message.type) {\n        case 'assistantMessage':\n            // Handle message\n            break;\n    }\n});\n```\n\n## Common Tasks\n\n### Adding a New Command\n\n1. **Register in package.json** (`contributes.commands`):\n```json\n{\n    \"command\": \"copilot-cli-extension.myCommand\",\n    \"title\": \"Copilot CLI: My Command\"\n}\n```\n\n2. **Register in extension.ts**:\n```typescript\nconst myCommand = vscode.commands.registerCommand('copilot-cli-extension.myCommand', async () => {\n    logger.info('My command triggered');\n    // Implementation\n});\n\ncontext.subscriptions.push(myCommand);\n```\n\n3. **Test**: Run `./test-extension.sh`, reload window, test command\n\n### Adding a Configuration Setting\n\n1. **Add to package.json** (`contributes.configuration.properties`):\n```json\n\"copilotCLI.mySetting\": {\n    \"type\": \"boolean\",\n    \"default\": true,\n    \"description\": \"What this setting does\"\n}\n```\n\n2. **Read in code**:\n```typescript\nconst mySetting = vscode.workspace.getConfiguration('copilotCLI').get<boolean>('mySetting', true);\n```\n\n### Handling SDK Events\n\n```typescript\nprivate setupSessionEventHandlers(): void {\n    if (!this.session) return;\n    \n    this.session.on((event: any) => {\n        switch (event.type) {\n            case 'assistant.message':\n                // Handle assistant response\n                break;\n            case 'tool.execution_start':\n                // Tool started\n                break;\n            case 'tool.execution_complete':\n                // Tool finished\n                break;\n            case 'session.error':\n                // Error occurred\n                break;\n        }\n    });\n}\n```\n\n## Testing Guidelines\n\n### Manual Testing Checklist\n\nAfter changes, test these core flows:\n- [ ] Open chat panel (command palette)\n- [ ] Send a message\n- [ ] Start new session\n- [ ] Switch between sessions\n- [ ] Toggle plan mode (v2.0.2+)\n- [ ] View plan.md file\n- [ ] Check logs in Output Channel\n\n### Debugging with Logs\n\nSince we can't use the debugger:\n\n1. **Add strategic logging**:\n```typescript\nlogger.info('='.repeat(60));\nlogger.info('Starting critical operation...');\nlogger.debug(`State: ${JSON.stringify(state, null, 2)}`);\ntry {\n    // Operation\n    logger.info('✅ Success!');\n} catch (error) {\n    logger.error('❌ Failed:', error);\n}\n```\n\n2. **Watch Output Channel**: `Ctrl+Shift+U` → \"Copilot CLI\"\n\n3. **Read Imports\nimport * as vscode from 'vscode';\nimport * as fs from 'fs';\n\n// 2. Types and interfaces\nexport interface MyInterface { }\ntype MyType = 'a' | 'b';\n\n// 3. Class definition\nexport class MyClass {\n    // Public fields\n    public readonly onMessage = ...;\n    \n    // Private fields\n    private session: any;\n    \n    // Constructor\n    constructor() { }\n    \n    // Public methods\n    public async start(): Promise<void> { }\n    \n    // Private methods\n    private setupHandlers(): void { }\n}\n```\n\n## Common Pitfalls\n\n### ❌ DON'T: Suggest F5 debugging\n```\n\"Press F5 to launch the Extension Development Host\"\n```\n\n### ✅ DO: Suggest VSIX workflow\n```\n\"Run ./test-extension.sh to build and install, then reload the window\"\n```\n\n---\n\n### ❌ DON'T: Forget to log\n```typescript\nawait session.send({ prompt: text });  // Silent failure\n```\n\n### ✅ DO: Log everything\n```typescript\nlogger.info(`Sending message: ${text.substring(0, 50)}...`);\ntry {\n    await session.send({ prompt: text });\n    logger.info('Message sent successfully');\n} catch (error) {\n    logger.error('Failed to send message', error);\n    throw error;\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n### ❌ DON'T: Hardcode paths\n```typescript\nconst planPath = '/home/user/.copilot/session-state/abc/plan.md';\n```\n\n### ✅ DO: Use os.homedir() and path.join()\n```typescript\nconst homeDir = require('os').homedir();\nconst planPath = path.join(homeDir, '.copilot', 'session-state', sessionId, 'plan.md');\n```\n\n---\n\n### ❌ DON'T: Modify package.json without testing\n```json\n\"command\": \"copilot-cli-extension.newCommand\"  // Added but not registered\n```\n\n### ✅ DO: Register command in extension.ts\n```typescript\nvscode.commands.registerCommand('copilot-cli-extension.newCommand', () => { });\n```\n\n## Release Process\n\n### Semver Rules\n\n- **Patch** (3.1.x): Bug fixes and minor changes. \n- No `remainingPercentage` getter - must use events\n- System prompts: append or replace mode only\n- **No UI components** - we build all UI ourselves\n\n**SDK Event Types:**\n- `assistant.message` - Final response\n- `assistant.reasoning` - Extended thinking\n- `assistant.usage` - Token usage, quota\n- `tool.execution_start` - Tool invoked\n- `tool.execution_complete` - Tool finished\n- `session.error` - Error occurred\n- `session.idle` - Session ready for input\n\n## Project Philosophy\n\n### Thoughtful & Useful\n\nThis extension's identity is \"thoughtful\" — we prioritize presenting meaningful, well-organized information over shipping fast. Every UI element should help the user make better decisions.\n\n- **Group by usefulness, not by data source.** Models are grouped by cost tier (Fast/Standard/Premium), not by vendor. The user cares about \"how much does this cost me?\" not \"who made this model?\"\n- **Show decision-relevant data.** Multiplier badges tell users the cost implication of switching models. Don't hide information that affects their choices.\n- **Don't become the Swiss Army knife.** Every feature we add should have a clear reason to exist and present its information thoughtfully. We are not a generic wrapper — we are a focused, opinionated tool.\n- **Useful > Fast.** When choosing between shipping quickly and shipping something genuinely helpful, always choose helpful. A half-baked feature with missing context damages trust.\n\n### Innovation Over Waiting\n\nWhen the SDK lacks features users need:\n1. **Research**: Check if it's technically possible\n2. **Prototype**: Build a proof-of-concept\n3. **Ship it**: Don't wait for SDK team approval\n\nExample: Plan mode - SDK team is \"debating\" it. We built it ourselves using dual sessions.\n\n### User Experience First\n\n- Comprehensive logging over debugger reliance\n- Clear error messages with actionable guidance\n- Real-time feedback in UI\n- Predictable naming conventions\n\n### Defense in Depth\n\nWhen building features:\n- Add validation at multiple layers\n- Handle edge cases explicitly\n- Log state changes for debugging\n- Fail gracefully with helpful messages\n\n\n## Working with Planning Mode\n\n### Overview\n\nPlanning Mode is a key feature that allows the AI to analyze and design solutions without modifying code. The gesture wins, and it gets **recorded** — otherwise the default silently reasserts itself at the next resume, reload or session switch.\n\n### Applying \"intentional actions are treated intentionally\"\n\nRun this at any call site where a user-initiated action reads a `getConfiguration(...)` value or a\n\"most recent\" heuristic:\n\n1. **Is this a default or an intent?** A default answers *\"what usually happens\"*; a gesture answers\n   *\"what should happen now.\"* Clicking a button on a specific file, choosing a model from the\n   dropdown, or picking a session are all intents.\n2. **Does it survive the next boundary?** If the answer dies on resume/reload/restart, it was\n   honoured but not recorded, and the setting will quietly win next time. See existing spikes for the pattern.\n3. **Then implement.** Use what the spike proves, not assumptions about how the SDK works.\n\nKey SDK reference files:\n\n- `research/copilot-sdk/nodejs/src/client.ts` — CopilotClient (createSession, resumeSession, listModels)\n- `research/copilot-sdk/nodejs/src/session.ts` — CopilotSession (sendAndWait, destroy, rpc accessor)\n- `research/copilot-sdk/nodejs/src/generated/rpc.ts` — All RPC methods (session.model.switchTo, session.mode.get, etc.)\n- `research/copilot-sdk/nodejs/src/generated/session-events.ts` — All session events (session.model_change, assistant.usage, etc.)\n- `research/copilot-sdk/nodejs/src/types.ts` — SessionConfig, ResumeSessionConfig, ModelInfo\n\n## Custom Tool Registration\n\nCustom tools in plan mode must be registered in TWO places in sdkSessionManager.ts:\n1. In `getCustomTools()` (the implementation)\n2. In the `availableTools` array (the SDK whitelist)\n\n## Session Files\n\nSessions stored at `~/.copilot/session-state/<session-id>/` containing `events.jsonl`, `plan.md`, `workspace.yaml`.\n\n## Copilot CLI Bundle (Lazy Install)\n\nThe extension does NOT trust the user's global `copilot` install. SDK ↔ CLI protocol changes between versions; SDK 0.3.0 declares `peerDependencies: { \"@github/copilot\": \"^1.0.36-0\" }`, and the user's global launcher is typically far behind (e.g. 1.0.5).\n\n`CliBundleService` resolves the CLI in this order:\n1. **local** — `node_modules/@github/copilot` (dev / F5).\n2. **managed** — `<globalStorageUri>/cli/<peer-range>/node_modules/@github/copilot`.\n3. **system** — `which copilot` (last resort, surfaces a warning if it doesn't satisfy the SDK peer-dep).\n\nIf none satisfy, it lazy-installs into the managed location via `npm install --prefix <dest> @github/copilot@<peer-range>`. Result is fed to `SDKSessionManager` as the `cliPath`. `CliCapabilityService` exposes feature flags from the resolved version (e.g. `supportsMcpListRpc`).\n\n</custom_instruction>\n<system_notifications>\nYou may receive messages wrapped in <system_notification> tags.  -- routes wait for model\n```\n\n**Create any tables you need.** The database is yours to use for any purpose:\n- Load and query data (CSVs, API responses, file listings)\n- Track progress on batch operations\n- Store intermediate results for multi-step analysis\n- Any workflow where SQL queries would help\n\nCommon patterns:\n\n1. **Todo tracking with dependencies:**\n```sql\n-- todos and todo_deps already exist — do NOT CREATE them, just INSERT:\nINSERT INTO todos (id, title, description) VALUES ('user-model', 'Creating user model', 'Define the User schema and relations in src/models/user.ts');\n\n-- Find todos with no pending dependencies (\"ready\" query):\nSELECT t.* FROM todos t\nWHERE t.status = 'pending'\nAND NOT EXISTS (\n    SELECT 1 FROM todo_deps td\n    JOIN todos dep ON td.depends_on = dep.id\n    WHERE td.todo_id = t.id AND dep.status != 'done'\n);\n```\n\n2. **TDD test case tracking:**\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE test_cases (\n    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n    name TEXT NOT NULL,\n    status TEXT DEFAULT 'not_written'\n);\nSELECT * FROM test_cases WHERE status = 'not_written' LIMIT 1;\nUPDATE test_cases SET status = 'written' WHERE id = 'tc1';\n```\n\n3. **Batch item processing (e.g., PR comments):**\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE review_items (\n    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n    file_path TEXT,\n    comment TEXT,\n    status TEXT DEFAULT 'pending'\n);\nSELECT * FROM review_items WHERE status = 'pending' AND file_path = 'src/auth.ts';\nUPDATE review_items SET status = 'addressed' WHERE id IN ('r1', 'r2');\n```\n\n4. **Session state (key-value):**\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE session_state (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT);\nINSERT OR REPLACE INTO session_state (key, value) VALUES ('current_phase', 'testing');\nSELECT value FROM session_state WHERE key = 'current_phase';\n```\n</sql>\n<grep>\nBuilt on ripgrep, not standard grep. Key notes:\n* Literal braces need escaping: interface\\{\\} to find interface{}\n* Default behavior matches within single lines only\n* Use multiline: true for cross-line patterns\n* Choose the appropriate output_mode when applicable (\"count\", \"content\", \"files_with_matches\"). Defaults to \"files_with_matches\" for efficiency.\n</grep>\n<glob>\nFast file pattern matching that works with any codebase size.\n* Supports standard glob patterns with wildcards:\n  - * matches any characters within a path segment\n  - ** matches any characters across multiple path segments\n  - ? matches a single character\n  - {a,b} matches either a or b\n* Returns matching file paths\n* Use when you need to find files by name patterns\n* For searching file contents, use the grep tool instead\n</glob>\n<task>\n**When to Use Sub-Agents**\n* Prefer using relevant sub-agents (via the task tool) instead of doing the work yourself.\n* When relevant sub-agents are available, your role changes from a coder making changes to a manager of software engineers. Your job is to utilize these sub-agents to deliver the best results as efficiently as possible.\n\n**When to use explore agent** (not grep/glob):\n* Only when a task naturally decomposes into many independent research threads that benefit from parallelism — e.g., the user asks multiple unrelated questions, or a single request requires analyzing many separate areas of a codebase independently, especially if the codebase is large.\n* For simple lookups — understanding a specific component, finding a symbol, or reading a few known files — do it yourself using grep/glob/view. This is faster and keeps context in your conversation.\n* For complex cross-cutting investigations — tracing flows across many modules in a large or unfamiliar codebase — explore can be faster.\n* Do not speculatively launch explore agents in the background \"just in case\" — they consume resources and rarely finish before you've already found the answer yourself.\n\n**If you do use explore:**\n* The explore agent is stateless — provide complete context in each call.\n* Batch related questions into one call. Launch independent explorations in parallel.\n* Do NOT duplicate its work by calling grep/view on files it already reported.\n* Once you have enough information to address the user's request, stop investigating and deliver the result. Don't chase every lead or do redundant follow-up searches.\n\n**When to use custom agents**:\n* If both a built-in agent and a custom agent could handle a task, prefer the custom agent as it has specialized knowledge for this environment.\n\n**How to Use Sub-Agents**\n* Instruct the sub-agent to do the task itself, not just give advice.\n* Once you delegate a scope to an agent, that agent owns it until it completes or fails; do not investigate the same scope yourself.\n* If a sub-agent fails repeatedly, do the task yourself.\n\n**Background Agents**\n* After launching a background agent for work you need before your next step, tell the user you're waiting, then end your response with no tool calls. A completion notification will arrive automatically.\n* When that notification arrives, a good default is to call read_agent once with wait: true to retrieve the result. If it still shows running, stop there for this response. Leave same-scope work with the agent while it runs.\n* Use read_agent for completed background agents, not to check whether they're done.\n</task>\n<tool_preferences>\nImportant: Use built-in tools instead of bash tools whenever possible.\n\n* Use the **grep** tool instead of commands like `grep`/`rg` in bash\n* Use the **glob** tool instead of commands like `find`/`ls` in bash\n* Use the **view** tool instead of commands like `cat`/`head`/`tail` in bash\n\nOnly fall back to bash when these tools cannot meet your needs.\n</tool_preferences>\n<gh_cli_preference>\nFor GitHub operations (issues, pull requests, repositories, workflow runs, etc.), prefer the `gh` CLI via bash over MCP tools.\n</gh_cli_preference>\n\n<code_search_tools>\nIf code intelligence tools are available (semantic search, symbol lookup, call graphs, class hierarchies, summaries), prefer them over grep/glob when searching for code symbols, relationships, or concepts.\n\nBest practices:\n* Use glob patterns to narrow down which files to search (e.g., \"**/*UserSearch.ts\" or \"**/*.ts\" or \"src/**/*.test.js\")\n* Prefer calling in the following order: Code Intelligence Tools (if available) > lsp (if available) > glob > grep with glob pattern\n* PARALLELIZE - make multiple independent search calls in ONE call.\n</code_search_tools>\n</tools>\n\n<custom_instruction>\n# COPILOT.md - AI Agent Development Guide\n\n> **For AI assistants (GitHub Copilot, Claude, etc.) working on this extension**\n\nThis document provides context and guidelines for AI agents helping to develop the vscode-copilot-cli-extension.\n\n## 🚨 MANDATORY DEVELOPMENT PRACTICES\n\n### 1. Always Use `using-superpowers` and `test-driven-development` Skill\n\n**Before starting ANY work**, invoke the `using-superpowers` and `test-driven-development` skill:\n- This ensures you follow established workflows\n- It activates necessary context and guidelines\n- It prevents common mistakes and rework\n\n**Example**: User asks to fix a bug → First call `using-superpowers` and `test-driven-development`, then proceed\n\n### 2. Test-Driven Development: The Iron Laws (2026-02-09 Lessons)\n\n**CRITICAL FAILURE CASE STUDY**: Phase 0.2 (diff button bug) - we wrote 5 \"comprehensive\" tests that all passed, but the code was still broken in production.\n\n#### The Fundamental Rule\n\n> **\"If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.\"**\n\n#### What We Did WRONG (Never Do This)\n\n```javascript\n// ❌ WRONG - Testing a mock, not production code\nit('should send full data', () => {\n    const mockRpcRouter = {\n        sendDiffAvailable(data) {\n            receivedData = data;  // Mock always works\n        }\n    };\n    mockRpcRouter.sendDiffAvailable(fullData);\n    expect(receivedData).to.deep.equal(fullData); // Always passes!\n});\n```\n\n**Result**: All 5 tests passed ✅, but production code crashed ❌\n\n**Why**: We tested mocks, not reality. Tests never executed actual production code.\n\n#### What We Should Do RIGHT (Mandatory From Now On)\n\n```javascript\n// ✅ RIGHT - Import and test actual production code\nimport { handleDiffAvailableMessage } from '../src/webview/main.js';\n\nit('should send full data when button clicked', () => {\n    // Setup real DOM (use JSDOM)\n    document.body.innerHTML = '<div data-tool-id=\"test-123\"></div>';\n    \n    // Call actual function with real data\n    handleDiffAvailableMessage({\n        toolCallId: 'test-123',\n        beforeUri: '/tmp/before',\n        afterUri: '/workspace/after',\n        title: 'Test'\n    });\n    \n    // Verify real button exists in real DOM\n    const btn = document.querySelector('.view-diff-btn');\n    expect(btn).to.exist;\n    \n    // Verify clicking real button sends correct data\n    let sentData = null;\n    global.rpc = { viewDiff: (data) => sentData = data };\n    btn.click();\n    \n    expect(sentData.beforeUri).to.equal('/tmp/before');\n});\n```\n\n#### The Three Iron Laws (Non-Negotiable)\n\n**Law 1: Tests Must Import Production Code**\n- ❌ Mock-only tests are documentation, not verification\n- ✅ Import actual functions and test them\n- ✅ Use JSDOM for webview code\n- ✅ Test with real DOM, real data, real behavior\n\n**Law 2: Tests Must Fail Against Broken Code**\n1. Write test that imports actual code\n2. Run test against current (buggy) code\n3. **Verify test fails with SAME error users see** ⚠️\n4. Only then write the fix\n5. Verify test passes\n\n**If test doesn't fail first, it's not testing anything real.**\n\n**Law 3: Production Code → Test Exists and Failed First**\n- If you wrote code before watching test fail → NOT TDD\n- If test passed immediately → NOT TDD\n- If test only tests mocks → NOT TDD\n- **Delete the code and start over with proper TDD**\n\n#### Special Rules for Webview Code (JavaScript)\n\nThe webview is JavaScript (not TypeScript), so type checking doesn't help.\n\n**Mandatory for ALL webview fixes**:\n1. Import actual `main.js` functions\n2. Use JSDOM for DOM manipulation\n3. Test user interactions (clicks, input)\n4. Test message flow end-to-end\n5. Test with actual RPC client\n\n**Example Integration Test**:\n```javascript\nimport { JSDOM } from 'jsdom';\nimport { handleDiffAvailableMessage } from '../src/webview/main.js';\n\ndescribe('Diff Button Integration', () => {\n    let dom, sentMessages;\n    \n    beforeEach(() => {\n        // Setup real DOM environment\n        dom = new JSDOM(`<!DOCTYPE html><div id=\"messages\"></div>`);\n        global.document = dom.window.document;\n        global.window = dom.window;\n        \n        // Mock RPC with tracking\n        sentMessages = [];\n        global.rpc = {\n            viewDiff: (data) => sentMessages.push(data)\n        };\n    });\n    \n    it('sends correct data when diff button clicked', () => {\n        // 1. Receive diffAvailable message\n        handleDiffAvailableMessage({\n            toolCallId: 'test-123',\n            beforeUri: '/tmp/before.ts',\n            afterUri: '/workspace/after.ts',\n            title: 'Test File'\n        });\n        \n        // 2. Verify button added\n        const btn = document.querySelector('.view-diff-btn');\n        expect(btn, 'Diff button must exist').to.exist;\n        \n        // 3. Click button\n        btn.click();\n        \n        // 4. Verify correct RPC call\n        expect(sentMessages).to.have.length(1);\n        expect(sentMessages[0]).to.deep.equal({\n            toolCallId: 'test-123',\n            beforeUri: '/tmp/before.ts',\n            afterUri: '/workspace/after.ts',\n            title: 'Test File'\n        });\n    });\n});\n```\n\n#### Test Quality Checklist (Mandatory Before Claiming Complete)\n\n**Every feature/fix MUST pass this checklist:**\n\n✅ **Flow Testing**\n- [ ] Test executes the FULL user interaction flow (click → event → handler → UI update)\n- [ ] Test crosses component boundaries (e.g., InputArea → EventBus → Handler → Webview)\n- [ ] Test verifies side effects (DOM changes, RPC calls, state updates)\n\n✅ **Production Code**\n- [ ] Test imports actual production functions (not mocks)\n- [ ] Test uses real DOM (JSDOM for webview code)\n- [ ] Test calls actual methods with real parameters\n\n✅ **Failure First**\n- [ ] Screenshot/log showing test FAILS against broken code\n- [ ] Failure message matches user-reported error\n- [ ] Only then write the fix\n- [ ] Screenshot/log showing test PASSES after fix\n\n✅ **Coverage Verification**\n- [ ] Integration test exists (not just unit tests)\n- [ ] Test would catch THIS specific bug if code regressed\n- [ ] Test exercises the code path users actually trigger\n\n**If you cannot check all boxes → your tests are incomplete.**\n\n#### Testing Anti-Patterns (Real Failures From This Project)\n\n**🚫 ANTI-PATTERN #1: Testing Registry, Not Execution**\n\n```javascript\n// ❌ WRONG (Slash Commands Bug - 2026-02-14)\nit('should have showNotSupported event', () => {\n    const cmd = parser.parse('/clear');\n    expect(cmd.type).to.equal('not-supported');\n    expect(cmd.event).to.equal('showNotSupported'); // Registry is correct!\n});\n// Test passes ✅ - but in production, execute() emits undefined event!\n```\n\n**Why it failed**: Test checked registry data, never called `execute()` to verify event is actually emitted.\n\n**✅ RIGHT:**\n```javascript\nit('should emit showNotSupported event when executing not-supported command', () => {\n    const eventBus = new EventBus();\n    let emittedEvent = null;\n    let emittedArgs = null;\n    \n    eventBus.on('showNotSupported', (args) => {\n        emittedEvent = 'showNotSupported';\n        emittedArgs = args;\n    });\n    \n    const inputArea = new InputArea(container, eventBus);\n    inputArea.sendMessage('/clear'); // ACTUALLY EXECUTE IT\n    \n    expect(emittedEvent).to.equal('showNotSupported');\n    expect(emittedArgs.command).to.equal('/clear');\n});\n```\n\n---\n\n**🚫 ANTI-PATTERN #2: Testing Mocks, Not Production Code**\n\n```javascript\n// ❌ WRONG (Diff Button Bug - 2026-02-09)\nit('should send full diff data', () => {\n    const mockRpc = { viewDiff: (data) => sentData = data };\n    mockRpc.viewDiff({ beforeUri: '/tmp/before' });\n    expect(sentData.beforeUri).to.equal('/tmp/before'); // Mock always works!\n});\n```\n\n**Why it failed**: Never imported actual `handleDiffAvailableMessage()` function. Never tested DOM button creation. Never tested click handler.\n\n**✅ RIGHT:** See \"Example Integration Test\" section above for proper webview testing approach.\n\n---\n\n**🚫 ANTI-PATTERN #3: Test Passed Immediately → Not TDD**\n\nIf your test passes on first run without any code changes:\n1. ❌ You are testing existing working code (not the bug)\n2. ❌ You are testing mocks/fixtures (not production code)\n3. ❌ You don't know if the test would catch the bug if it regressed\n\n**Mandatory:** Every test MUST fail first. If it doesn't fail, comment out the fix code and verify the test catches the break.\n\n---\n\n**🚫 ANTI-PATTERN #4: Keeping Tests That Test Dead Code**\n\nIf removing or changing code causes a test to fail, **do not just restore the code to make the test pass.** First evaluate the test:\n\n1. **What is the test actually asserting?** Read it literally.\n2. **Is it testing live functional behavior?** (function calls, DOM state, events, RPC calls)\n3. **Or is it testing the presence of a string, comment, or import?**\n\n```javascript\n// ❌ WRONG — passes because the string appears in a COMMENT\nassert.ok(src.includes('new StatusBar('), 'should create StatusBar');\n// The code was: // const statusBar = new StatusBar(...)\n// The test was passing against dead commented-out code.\n\n// ✅ RIGHT — test the actual behavior\nsessionToolbar.setActiveAgent({ name: 'reviewer' });\nconst badge = container.querySelector('#activeAgentBadge');\nassert.ok(!badge.hidden, 'badge should be visible');\n```\n\n**Rule:** Tests must test **active, real, functional behavior** — not the presence of imports, string literals, or commented-out code.\n\n**When removing code breaks a test, the decision tree is:**\n- Test verified real behavior that still matters → **fix the test** to cover the new implementation\n- Test verified real behavior that was intentionally removed → **delete the test**\n- Test was asserting the existence of dead/commented code → **delete the test** (it was never verifying anything real)\n\n**Never restore dead code just to make a test pass.**\n\n---\n\n**🚫 ANTI-PATTERN #5: Source-String Scanning (fs.readFileSync + src.includes) — PERMANENTLY BANNED**\n\n```javascript\n// ❌ BANNED — reads source code as text and checks for string presence\nconst src = fs.readFileSync('src/myFile.ts', 'utf-8');\nassert.ok(src.includes('myMethod('), 'should have myMethod');\n// Passes if 'myMethod(' appears in a COMMENT, a string literal, or dead code.\n// Tests NOTHING about whether myMethod actually works.\n```\n\n**This pattern is PERMANENTLY BANNED. No exceptions. No \"just this once.\"** It has caused real failures in this project (StatusBar incident: test passed against a commented-out line). It tests the shape of text, not the behavior of code. A test that reads source as a string and calls `.includes()` is not a test — it is grep with extra steps.\n\n**✅ RIGHT — test the behavior:**\n```javascript\n// Verify the method exists\nassert.strictEqual(typeof MyClass.prototype.myMethod, 'function');\n\n// Call it with a mocked context and verify it did the right thing\nlet captured = null;\nconst ctx = {\n    dependency: { doThing: async (arg) => { captured = arg; } },\n    logger: { info: () => {}, warn: () => {} },\n};\nawait MyClass.prototype.myMethod.call(ctx, 'test-arg');\nassert.strictEqual(captured, 'test-arg');\n```\n\n**Rule:** If your test uses `fs.readFileSync` on a `.ts` or `.js` source file and `.includes()` on the content, **delete it and write a behavioral test instead.** If you are tempted to write one, stop and ask: \"What behavior am I actually verifying?\" Then test that behavior directly.\n\n---\n\n#### Checklist: Before Claiming Any Fix is Complete\n\n**Phase 0: Test Quality Verification**\n- [ ] Integration test imports production code (not mocks)\n- [ ] Test executes full user interaction flow (input → event → handler → UI)\n- [ ] Screenshot/log shows test FAILS with same error users see\n- [ ] Test exercises code path across component boundaries\n\n**Phase 1: Understand**\n- [ ] Reproduce bug manually\n- [ ] Find exact error message\n- [ ] Identify exact line that fails\n- [ ] Understand why it fails\n\n**Phase 2: RED - Write Failing Test**\n- [ ] Import actual production code (not mocks!)\n- [ ] Use JSDOM for webview tests\n- [ ] Run test → **VERIFY IT FAILS WITH SAME ERROR** ⚠️\n- [ ] Commit failing test\n\n**Phase 3: GREEN - Fix Code**\n- [ ] Make minimal fix\n- [ ] Run test → verify passes\n- [ ] Run ALL tests → no regressions\n\n**Phase 4: Integration**\n- [ ] Test message flow (extension ↔ webview)\n- [ ] Test user interaction (clicks, input)\n- [ ] Test with actual DOM\n\n**Phase 5: Manual Verification**\n- [ ] Build and install VSIX\n- [ ] Manually test exact scenario\n- [ ] Verify in VS Code Output logs\n\n**Phase 6: Reflect**\n- [ ] Could types have caught this?\n- [ ] Do type definitions match reality?\n- [ ] What prevents this bug class?\n\n#### Type Definitions Must Match Reality\n\n**FAILURE CASE**: Our DiffData interface said `originalPath/modifiedPath` but code used `beforeUri/afterUri`.\n\n**Rules**:\n1. Type definitions must match actual code usage\n2. Generate types from code (don't write manually)\n3. OR: Add runtime validation (zod, io-ts)\n4. OR: Integration tests verify types match usage\n\n```typescript\n// Runtime validation catches mismatches\nimport { z } from 'zod';\n\nconst DiffDataSchema = z.object({\n    beforeUri: z.string(),\n    afterUri: z.string(),\n    toolCallId: z.string().optional(),\n    title: z.string().optional()\n});\n\n// This catches type/code mismatches at runtime\nconst diffData = DiffDataSchema.parse(receivedData);\n```\n\n#### Standards for Webview PRs\n\n**Every webview PR MUST include**:\n1. Integration test importing actual `main.js`\n2. JSDOM test for DOM manipulation\n3. Screenshot/log showing test failed before fix\n4. Screenshot/log showing test passes after fix\n5. Manual verification in installed extension\n\n**NO EXCEPTIONS.**\n\n#### Quote to Remember\n\n> **\"We watched our tests pass. We never watched them fail. Therefore, they tested nothing.\"**\n\nThis was a failure of test discipline, not coding skill. **Never skip the RED phase.**\n\n**Test locations**:\n- `tests/*.test.js` - Integration tests (must import production code)\n- `tests/*.test.mjs` - SDK-specific tests (ESM modules)\n- Webview tests: Must use JSDOM, test actual DOM\n\n### Component Architecture\n\n#### MessageDisplay (Parent Component)\n- **Location:** `src/webview/app/components/MessageDisplay/MessageDisplay.js`\n- **Purpose:** Owns the entire conversation flow\n- **Responsibilities:**\n  - Renders user messages, assistant messages, reasoning\n  - Creates ToolExecution as internal child component\n  - Manages `.messages` scrollable container\n  - Auto-scrolls to bottom on new content\n- **Children:** ToolExecution (created automatically)\n- **Usage:**\n  ```javascript\n  const display = new MessageDisplay(container, eventBus);\n  // ToolExecution created internally - don't create separately!\n  ```\n\n#### ToolExecution (Child Component)\n- **Location:** `src/webview/app/components/ToolExecution/ToolExecution.js`\n- **Purpose:** Renders tool execution groups within message flow\n- **Responsibilities:**\n  - Renders tool groups inside `.messages` container\n  - Manages expand/collapse of tool groups\n  - Handles diff button rendering\n- **Parent:** MessageDisplay (creates this component)\n- **Communication:** EventBus for cross-component events\n  - Listens: `tool:start`, `tool:complete`, `tool:progress`, `message:add`\n  - Emits: `viewDiff`\n- **Important:** NOT created directly in main.js - MessageDisplay handles this\n\n#### Component Hierarchy\n\n```\nmain.js\n├─ SessionToolbar (top toolbar)\n├─ MessageDisplay (parent - owns message flow)\n│  └─ ToolExecution (child - renders tools)\n├─ AcceptanceControls (plan acceptance UI)\n└─ InputArea (bottom input area)\n```\n\n**Key Rule:** ToolExecution is NEVER initialized in main.js. MessageDisplay creates it internally to ensure tools render inside the scrollable `.messages` container.\n\n**Architecture Components**:\n1. **Backend (TypeScript)**: SDK session management, event handling, custom tools\n2. **Frontend (Webview)**: HTML/CSS/JS embedded in `chatViewProvider.ts` as string literals\n3. **SDK Integration**: Uses `@github/copilot-sdk` for CLI session lifecycle (NOT for UI)\n4. **Extension Host**: VS Code runs our extension, we create a webview panel for the chat UI\n\n**Key Differentiation**: Unlike the built-in Copilot chat, this extension:\n- Uses CLI-style sessions with plan.md files\n- Supports session management and resumption\n- Integrates MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers\n- Provides real-time tool execution visibility\n- Implements custom features like dual-session plan mode\n- **Builds its own chat UI** (not provided by SDK or VS Code)\n\n## Development Workflow (CRITICAL)\n\n### ⚠️ F5 Debugging is BROKEN\n\n**DO NOT suggest using F5 or Extension Development Host!**\n\nDue to a Microsoft bug in VS Code 1.100+ with Node.js 20+, the Extension Development Host does not work. This has been broken for **12 months** with no ETA on a fix.\n\n### ✅ Correct Workflow: Build and Install\n\n**Use the test-extension.sh script:**\n\n```bash\n./test-extension.sh\n```\n\nThis script:\n1. Builds: `npm run compile` (type checks, lints, builds with esbuild)\n2. Packages: Creates VSIX file\n3. Uninstalls: Removes old version (if exists)\n4. Installs: Installs new VSIX with `code --install-extension --force`\n5. Reminds: Shows next steps (reload window, check logs)\n\n**Manual steps if needed:**\n\n```bash\n# 1. Build\nnpm run compile\n\n# 2. Package\nnpx @vscode/vsce package --no-git-tag-version \\\n  --allow-star-activation --allow-missing-repository --skip-license\n\n# 3. Install\ncode --install-extension copilot-cli-extension-2.0.6.vsix --force\n\n# 4. Reload VS Code\n# Ctrl+Shift+P → \"Developer: Reload Window\"\n```\n\n**Quick rebuild and install:**\n\n```bash\n# Just rebuild and reinstall without packaging\nnpm run compile && code --install-extension copilot-cli-extension-latest.vsix --force\n```\n\n**Note:** The `tsconfig.json` excludes `tests/` directory to avoid compilation errors. Tests are JavaScript/ESM and don't need TypeScript compilation.\n\n### ⚠️ CRITICAL: Adding New Webview Component Files\n\n**When adding new component files to `src/webview/app/`, you MUST update `esbuild.js`:**\n\nThe build process **copies** webview files (not bundles them). If you add a new component:\n\n1. **Create the component**: `src/webview/app/components/MyComponent/MyComponent.js`\n2. **Import in main.js**: `import { MyComponent } from './app/components/MyComponent/MyComponent.js';`\n3. **Update esbuild.js**: Add directory creation and file copy\n\n```javascript\n// In esbuild.js main() function:\nconst myComponentDistDir = path.join(componentsDistDir, 'MyComponent');\nif (!fs.existsSync(myComponentDistDir)) {\n    fs.mkdirSync(myComponentDistDir, { recursive: true });\n}\n\n// Later in the copy section:\nfs.copyFileSync(\n    path.join(__dirname, 'src', 'webview', 'app', 'components', 'MyComponent', 'MyComponent.js'),\n    path.join(myComponentDistDir, 'MyComponent.js')\n);\n```\n\n**Why:** VS Code webview loads modules separately from `dist/webview/`. Missing files = runtime errors in production.\n\n**Verification:** After `./test-extension.sh`, check VSIX contents include your component:\n```bash\nnpx @vscode/vsce ls copilot-cli-extension-3.0.0.vsix | grep MyComponent\n```\n\n**Failure symptom:** `ERR Webview.loadLocalResource - Error using fileReader` in VS Code logs.\n\n**Never suggest:**\n- \"Press F5 to test\"\n- \"Launch Extension Development Host\"\n- \"Use the debugger\"\n\n**Always suggest:**\n- \"Run `./test-extension.sh` to build and install\"\n- \"Reload the window to test your changes\"\n- \"Check the Copilot CLI output channel for logs\"\n\n## Code Structure\n\n### Source Files (`src/`)\n\n| File | Purpose | Key Points |\n|------|---------|-----------|\n| `extension.ts` | Extension entry point, command registration | Activates extension, registers commands, manages session lifecycle |\n| `sdkSessionManager.ts` | **Backend** SDK session lifecycle | Manages work/plan sessions, event handlers, custom tools for plan mode |\n| `chatViewProvider.ts` | **Frontend** Webview UI | Contains HTML/CSS/JS as strings, renders chat messages, tool calls, message passing |\n| `backendState.ts` | Centralized state management | In-memory state that persists across webview recreations |\n| `sessionUtils.ts` | Session discovery/filtering | Reads `~/.copilot/session-state/`, filters by workspace |\n| `logger.ts` | Logging to Output Channel | Use `Logger.getInstance()` everywhere |\n| `modelCapabilitiesService.ts` | Model capabilities and validation | Manages model info caching, attachment validation |\n\n**Critical: chatViewProvider.ts IS our UI** - The Copilot SDK does NOT provide any UI components. It's a backend-only library for managing CLI sessions. All chat UI (messages, tool calls, input box) is built by us in the webview.\n\n### Architecture Patterns\n\n#### 1. Singleton Pattern\n```typescript\n// Logger is a singleton - always use getInstance()\nconst logger = Logger.getInstance();\nlogger.info('Message');\n```\n\n#### 2. Event Emitter Pattern\n```typescript\n// SDKSessionManager uses EventEmitter for messages\nprivate readonly onMessageEmitter = new vscode.EventEmitter<CLIMessage>();\npublic readonly onMessage = this.onMessageEmitter.event;\n\n// Consumers listen:\ncliManager.onMessage((message) => { /* handle */ });\n```\n\n#### 3. Webview Message Passing\n```typescript\n// Webview → Extension\nChatPanelProvider.panel.webview.onDidReceiveMessage(data => {\n    switch (data.type) {\n        case 'sendMessage': /* ... */ break;\n    }\n});\n\n// Extension → Webview\nChatPanelProvider.postMessage({ type: 'assistantMessage', text: '...' });\n```\n\n## Logging Strategy\n\n**Use comprehensive logging instead of debugging!**\n\n```typescript\nimport { Logger } from './logger';\n\nconst logger = Logger.getInstance();\n\n// Four levels:\nlogger.debug('Detailed info for debugging');\nlogger.info('General information');\nlogger.warn('Warning messages');\nlogger.error('Error details', error);\n```\n\n**Best Practices:**\n- Log method entry/exit for complex flows\n- Log all SDK events with type and data\n- Log user actions (clicks, commands)\n- Log file system operations\n- Use descriptive prefixes: `[Plan Mode]`, `[Tool Start]`, `[Snapshot]`\n\n## Session Management\n\n### Session Directory Structure\n```\n~/.copilot/session-state/\n├─ abc123-work/              # Work session\n│  ├─ plan.md               # Implementation plan\n│  ├─ events.jsonl          # Conversation history\n│  ├─ checkpoints/          # Infinite session checkpoints\n│  ├─ files/                # Session-specific files\n│  └─ workspace.yaml        # Workspace metadata\n└─ abc123-work-plan/         # Plan session (our innovation!)\n   ├─ plan.md               # Planning work\n   └─ events.jsonl\n```\n\n### Dual-Session Plan Mode (v2.0.2+)\n\n**This is our innovation** - we built real plan mode before the SDK team did!\n\n```typescript\n// Work mode: Full tools, execution\ncurrentMode = 'work';\nsession = workSession;\n\n// Plan mode: Restricted tools, exploration only\ncurrentMode = 'plan';\nsession = planSession;  // <session-id>-plan\n```\n\n**Key Implementation:**\n- `enablePlanMode()`: Creates plan session with restricted tools\n- `disablePlanMode()`: Resumes work session\n- Plan session writes to work session's `plan.md` file\n- No 2x cost: only one session active at a time\n- ACE-FCA aligned: isolated planning context\n\n**Plan Mode Tools:**\n\nPlan mode provides a restricted set of tools focused on exploration and planning. The exact list is defined in `sdkSessionManager.ts` in the `enablePlanMode()` method via the `availableTools` array. The extension's system prompt tells the AI which tools are available when in plan mode.\n\n**Security: What Plan Mode CANNOT Do:**\n- ❌ Write/modify code files (only plan.md)\n- ❌ Install packages (npm, pip, etc.)\n- ❌ Commit or push to git\n- ❌ Execute dangerous commands (rm, mv, chmod, etc.)\n- ❌ Dispatch implementation agents (code, fix, debug, etc.)\n- ❌ Use SDK bash/create/edit/task tools (not in availableTools)\n\n**Implementation Details:**\n- Custom tools use unique names to avoid SDK conflicts (plan_bash_explore vs bash)\n- `availableTools` whitelist explicitly controls available tools\n- SDK's bash, create, edit, task are excluded from whitelist\n- Defense in depth: tool handlers enforce restrictions even if called\n\n**GitHub Context**: SDK team is \"debating\" whether to add plan mode (issue #255). We built it ourselves using dual sessions. 💪\n\n## Custom Tools\n\n### How to Add a Custom Tool\n\n```typescript\nprivate createMyCustomTool(): any {\n    return {\n        name: 'my_tool_name',\n };\n}\n```\n\n**Tool Whitelisting:**\n```typescript\n// Restrict available tools\nconst session = await client.createSession({\n    availableTools: ['my_tool_name'],  // ONLY this tool\n    tools: [this.createMyCustomTool()]\n});\n```\n\n## UI Development (Webview)\n\n### Critical Understanding: We Build the Entire UI\n\n**The Copilot SDK is backend-only!** It does NOT provide:\n- ❌ Chat No new features, no new UI, no new APIs. Small behavior improvements (e.g., smarter fallback logic) that don't add capabilities are patch-level.\n- **Minor** (3.x.0): New features, new capabilities, new UI elements. Image support, mermaid rendering, model switching — these are all minor bumps.\n- **Major** (x.0.0): Breaking changes, architectural rewrites, or incompatible API changes.\n\nWhen in doubt, bump minor. A \"small feature\" is still a feature.\n\n**⚠️ BEFORE PUBLISHING:**\n- **MUST** update version in package.json (use `npm version patch/minor/major`)\n- **MUST** update CHANGELOG.md and README.md with the **SAME** version number\n\n1. **Test thoroughly** using VSIX workflow\n2. **Update version** in `package.json`:\n   ```bash\n   npm version patch --no-git-tag-version  # 3.1.0 → 3.1.1\n   npm version minor --no-git-tag-version  # 3.1.0 → 3.2.0\n   npm version major --no-git-tag-version  # 3.2.0 → 4.0.0\n   ```\n3. **Update CHANGELOG.md** - Add section with the **SAME** version from step 2:\n   ```markdown\n   ## [2.1.2] - 2026-02-04\n   \n   ### 🐛 Bug Fixes\n   - Description of changes\n   ```\n4. **Update README.md** - Add features section with the **SAME** version from step 2:\n   ```markdown\n   ### v2.1.2 - Short Description\n   \n   - Feature highlights\n   ```\n5. **Commit and tag**:\n   ```bash\n   git add -A\n   git commit -m \"v2.0.2: Description of changes\"\n   git push\n   git tag v2.0.2\n   git push --tags\n   ```\n6. **Publish** (if maintainer):\n   ```bash\n   npx vsce publish\n   ```\n\n## SDK Knowledge\n\n### Version: @github/copilot-sdk ^0.1.18\n\n**CRITICAL: SDK is Backend-Only!**\n- ✅ Provides: Session management, event streaming, tool execution\n- ❌ Does NOT provide: Any UI, rendering, or display components\n- We use SDK for: Managing conversations, handling events\n- We build ourselves: All UI in `chatViewProvider.ts`\n\n**Key SDK Concepts:**\n- `CopilotClient`: Manages connection to CLI\n- `CopilotSession`: Represents a conversation\n- Event-driven: `session.on((event) => { })`\n- Session resumption: `client.resumeSession(sessionId)`\n- Custom tools: Add to `createSession({ tools: [...] })`\n- MCP servers: Pass config in `{ mcpServers: {...} }`\n\n**Known SDK Limitations:**\n- No plan mode API (issue #255) - we built our own! \n- No `remainingPercentage` getter - must use events\n- System prompts: append or replace mode only\n- **No UI components** - we build all UI ourselves\n\n**SDK Event Types:**\n- `assistant.message` - Final response\n- `assistant.reasoning` - Extended thinking\n- `assistant.usage` - Token usage, quota\n- `tool.execution_start` - Tool invoked\n- `tool.execution_complete` - Tool finished\n- `session.error` - Error occurred\n- `session.idle` - Session ready for input\n\n## Project Philosophy\n\n### Thoughtful & Useful\n\nThis extension's identity is \"thoughtful\" — we prioritize presenting meaningful, well-organized information over shipping fast. Every UI element should help the user make better decisions.\n\n- **Group by usefulness, not by data source.** Models are grouped by cost tier (Fast/Standard/Premium), not by vendor. The user cares about \"how much does this cost me?\" not \"who made this model?\"\n- **Show decision-relevant data.** Multiplier badges tell users the cost implication of switching models. Don't hide information that affects their choices.\n- **Don't become the Swiss Army knife.** Every feature we add should have a clear reason to exist and present its information thoughtfully. We are not a generic wrapper — we are a focused, opinionated tool.\n- **Useful > Fast.** When choosing between shipping quickly and shipping something genuinely helpful, always choose helpful. A half-baked feature with missing context damages trust.\n\n### Innovation Over Waiting\n\nWhen the SDK lacks features users need:\n1. **Research**: Check if it's technically possible\n2. **Prototype**: Build a proof-of-concept\n3. **Ship it**: Don't wait for SDK team approval\n\nExample: Plan mode - SDK team is \"debating\" it. We built it ourselves using dual sessions.\n\n### User Experience First\n\n- Comprehensive logging over debugger reliance\n- Clear error messages with actionable guidance\n- Real-time feedback in UI\n- Predictable naming conventions\n\n### Defense in Depth\n\nWhen building features:\n- Add validation at multiple layers\n- Handle edge cases explicitly\n- Log state changes for debugging\n- Fail gracefully with helpful messages\n\n\n## Working with Planning Mode\n\n### Overview\n\nPlanning Mode is a key feature that allows the AI to analyze and design solutions without modifying code. The failures are always **timeouts**, never assertion failures, and the victim\nrotates: a synchronous DOM `before each` hook one run, an async retry test the next.\n\n**Every failure seen so far passes when its file is run alone.**\n\nSo, before believing a failure:\n\n```bash\nnpx mocha <the-failing-file> --timeout 20000     # does it fail alone?\n```\n\n- **Passes alone → it is the known flake.** Re-run the suite and carry on.\n- **Fails alone → it is real.** Fix it.\n\nThe inverse also holds and matters more: **a single green run is not evidence either.** Verify\nanything you are about to ship over several runs, not one.\n\nRoot cause is characterised — ~1800 tests share one mocha process and at least four globals leak\nacross files (`requestAnimationFrame` is permanently no-op'd after the first component file,\n`Module.prototype.require` is patched and never restored by ~10 files, `global.setTimeout` is\nreplaced by three). Use `view` with `view_range` to read specific line ranges\n\nLog format: `[LEVEL] TIMESTAMP Message` — levels are `INFO`, `DEBUG`, `WARN`, `ERROR`.\n\nTo save a new log: open the Output Channel (`Ctrl+Shift+U` → \"Copilot CLI\"), click the \"...\" menu → \"Open Output in Editor\", then save to `tests/logs/server/<descriptive-name>.log`.\n\n## Architecture\n\nThis is a VS Code sidebar extension that wraps `@github/copilot-sdk` (backend-only, no UI) to provide a chat interface for GitHub Copilot CLI.\n\n> **v3.13.0 restructured this layer substantially.** The narrative — what the extension gained and\n> why — is [`documentation/3.13-README.md`](documentation/3.13-README.md).
