to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.\n\n## Branding\n\nDo not add \"written by Claude Code\", \"generated by Claude\", \"Co-Authored-By: Claude\", or any AI attribution text to code, comments, commit messages, documentation, or any other output. The extension is built with Claude but branded as the user's own work.\n\n## Build & Test Commands\n\n```bash\nnpm run compile          # Type-check + lint + esbuild bundle\nnpm run watch            # Continuous rebuild (esbuild + tsc in parallel)\nnpm run package          # Production build (minified)\nnpm test                 # All unit + integration tests (~710 tests, Mocha + Chai)\nnpm run test:unit        # Unit tests only\nnpm run test:integration # Integration tests only\nnpm run check-types      # TypeScript type checking only\nnpm run lint             # ESLint on src/ (TypeScript only)\n./test-extension.sh      # Build → package VSIX → uninstall old → install new\n```\n\nRun single test file: `npx mocha tests/unit/components/some-test.test.js --timeout 10000`\n\n### The suite is flaky — a single red run proves nothing\n\n`npm test` fails on **most** full runs (measured: 6/6 consecutive runs, 1–2 failures each, no code\nchanges between them). The failures are always **timeouts**, never assertion failures, and the victim\nrotates: a synchronous DOM `before each` hook one run, an async retry test the next.\n\n**Every failure seen so far passes when its file is run alone.**\n\nSo, before believing a failure:\n\n```bash\nnpx mocha <the-failing-file> --timeout 20000     # does it fail alone?\n```\n\n- **Passes alone → it is the known flake.** Re-run the suite and carry on.\n- **Fails alone → it is real.** Fix it.\n\nThe inverse also holds and matters more: **a single green run is not evidence either.** Verify\nanything you are about to ship over several runs, not one.\n\nRoot cause is characterised — ~1800 tests share one mocha process and at least four globals leak\nacross files (`requestAnimationFrame` is permanently no-op'd after the first component file,\n`Module.prototype.require` is patched and never restored by ~10 files, `global.setTimeout` is\nreplaced by three). Three attempted fixes each surfaced a different problem, so it needs a design\ndecision rather than another patch. Evidence and options:\n`planning/backlog/test-suite-flake-cross-file-global-pollution.md`.\n\n## Debugging\n\n**F5 works.** The extension bundle has no `navigator` references, and the launch.json is correctly configured for `extensionHost`. Press F5 to launch the Extension Development Host. The preLaunchTask runs `npm run compile` (type-check + lint + esbuild).\n\nFor a faster dev loop, use `npm run watch` in a terminal and the VSIX workflow: `./test-extension.sh` then reload the window (`Ctrl+Shift+P` → \"Developer: Reload Window\").\n\nLogs go to the \"Copilot CLI\" Output Channel (`Ctrl+Shift+U`).\n\n### Saved Log Files\n\nThe `tests/logs/server/` directory contains log files manually saved from the Output Channel for debugging and documentation. To read them as an AI agent:\n\n1. Use `grep` to search for specific events (e.g., `grep -i \"model switch\\|error\\|warn\" tests/logs/server/model-change.log`)\n2. Use `head`/`tail` via bash for large files (they can exceed the `view` tool's size limit)\n3. Use `view` with `view_range` to read specific line ranges\n\nLog format: `[LEVEL] TIMESTAMP Message` — levels are `INFO`, `DEBUG`, `WARN`, `ERROR`.\n\nTo save a new log: open the Output Channel (`Ctrl+Shift+U` → \"Copilot CLI\"), click the \"...\" menu → \"Open Output in Editor\", then save to `tests/logs/server/<descriptive-name>.log`.\n\n## Architecture\n\nThis is a VS Code sidebar extension that wraps `@github/copilot-sdk` (backend-only, no UI) to provide a chat interface for GitHub Copilot CLI.\n\n> **v3.13.0 restructured this layer substantially.** The narrative — what the extension gained and\n> why — is [`documentation/3.13-README.md`](documentation/3.13-README.md). Read it before making\n> structural changes here.\n\n### Extension Host (TypeScript, `src/`)\n\n- **extension.ts** — Composition root. Registers commands, builds the registry, the sidebar surface and the panel service, wires SDK events to the owning host.\n- **sdkSessionManager.ts** — SDK session lifecycle. Creates/resumes CopilotClient sessions, streams messages, emits 15 granular events (onDidReceiveOutput, onDidStartTool, onDidProduceDiff, etc.).\n- **chatViewProvider.ts** — The sidebar's registration with VS Code, and nothing else (38 lines). `resolveWebviewView` hands its view to a `WebviewChatSurface` as a `SidebarSlot`.\n- **backendState.ts** — `SessionState` (one per conversation) and `WorkspaceRuntimeState` (one per window, observable). The `BackendState` facade over both is legacy and has no callers left in `extension.ts`.\n\n**The session layer** — free of `vscode` and SDK imports, so it is requirable from plain mocha and portable to v4.0. Hold that:\n\n- **src/extension/session/ChatSessionHost.ts** — one conversation, owned end to end. Its manager is a true `#private` field; the public surface follows ACP's verbs.\n- **src/extension/session/ChatSessionRegistry.ts** — which sessions are live in this window. `get()` probes without creating; `getOrCreate()` may bring one into being.\n- **sessionStartPlan / startManager / sessionBootstrap** — what a start request means, who it is for, and where its results land.\n\n**The surface layer:**\n\n- **src/extension/webview/webviewChatSurface.ts** — one chat surface: a webview, its RPC router, and the session it shows. N instances.\n- **src/extension/webview/chatWebviewSlot.ts** — the four members by which a sidebar view and an editor panel differ. `SidebarSlot` and `PanelSlot`.\n- **src/extension/webview/chatPanelService.ts** — opens, restores and closes chat tabs.\n- **src/extension/rpc/ExtensionRpcRouter.ts** — type-safe RPC, **one router per surface**. Extension side of the message bridge.\n- **src/extension/rpc/registerChatHandlers.ts** — wires one surface's handlers. Call once per router.\n- **src/extension/services/** — extracted services: SessionService, InlineDiffService, FileSnapshotService, MCPConfigurationService, ModelCapabilitiesService, PlanModeToolsService, MessageEnhancementService, sessionTranscriptBuilder, CopilotClientProvider, and others.\n\n### Webview (JavaScript ES modules, `src/webview/`)\n\nThe webview is plain JavaScript (not TypeScript, not bundled). Files are copied to `dist/` by esbuild.js.\n\n- **main.js** — Bootstrap. Creates components, wires EventBus, registers RPC handlers.\n- **app/rpc/WebviewRpcClient.js** — Webview-side RPC client using `acquireVsCodeApi()`.\n- **app/state/EventBus.js** — Pub/sub for loose component coupling.\n- **app/components/** — 9 components: MessageDisplay, ToolExecution, InputArea, SessionToolbar, AcceptanceControls, StatusBar, ActiveFileDisplay, PlanModeControls, SlashCommandPanel.\n- **app/handlers/** — 5 handler modules for UI events, acceptance, messages, diffs, tool groups.\n\n### Shared Types (`src/shared/`)\n\n- **messages.ts** — 31 RPC message type definitions (the contract between extension and webview).\n- **models.ts** — Domain types (Session, Message, ToolState, PlanModeStatus).\n\n### Data Flow\n\n```\nUser types message → InputArea → EventBus → main.js → WebviewRpcClient._send()\n  → postMessage → ExtensionRpcRouter handler → SDKSessionManager.sendMessage()\n  → Copilot SDK → CLI backend\n\nCLI responds → SDK event → SDKSessionManager emitter\n  → ChatViewProvider handler → ExtensionRpcRouter.send*()\n  → postMessage → WebviewRpcClient handler → EventBus.emit() → Components update DOM\n```\n\n### Key Patterns\n\n- **BufferedEmitter** (`src/utilities/bufferedEmitter.ts`): Queues events if webview isn't ready; replays on connect. Prevents lost messages during startup.\n- **DisposableStore** (`src/utilities/disposable.ts`): Centralized cleanup for subscriptions.\n- **Dual-session plan mode**: Work session + plan session. Plan session writes to work session's `plan.md`. Plan mode restricts tool access (no write/commit/install).\n\n## Versioning (Semver)\n\n- **Patch** (3.1.x): Bug fixes and minor changes. No new features, no new UI, no new APIs. Small behavior improvements (e.g., smarter fallback logic) that don't add capabilities are patch-level.\n- **Minor** (3.x.0): New features, new capabilities, new UI elements. Image support, mermaid rendering, model switching — these are all minor bumps.\n- **Major** (x.0.0): Breaking changes, architectural rewrites, or incompatible API changes.\n\nWhen in doubt, bump minor. A \"small feature\" is still a feature.\n\n## Design Principle: Thoughtful & Useful\n\nThis extension's identity is \"thoughtful\" — we prioritize presenting meaningful, well-organized information over shipping fast. Every UI element should help the user make better decisions.\n\n- **Group by usefulness, not by data source.** Models are grouped by cost tier (Fast/Standard/Premium), not by vendor. The user cares about \"how much does this cost me?\" not \"who made this model?\"\n- **Show decision-relevant data.** Multiplier badges tell users the cost implication of switching models. Don't hide information that affects their choices.\n- **Don't become the Swiss Army knife.** Every feature we add should have a clear reason to exist and present its information thoughtfully. We are not a generic wrapper — we are a focused, opinionated tool.\n- **Useful > Fast.** When choosing between shipping quickly and shipping something genuinely helpful, always choose helpful. A half-baked feature with missing context damages trust.\n- **Intentional actions are treated intentionally.** A setting is a standing default; a gesture is a stated intent. The gesture wins, and it gets **recorded** — otherwise the default silently reasserts itself at the next resume, reload or session switch.\n\n### Applying \"intentional actions are treated intentionally\"\n\nRun this at any call site where a user-initiated action reads a `getConfiguration(...)` value or a\n\"most recent\" heuristic:\n\n1. **Is this a default or an intent?** A default answers *\"what usually happens\"*; a gesture answers\n   *\"what should happen now.\"* Clicking a button on a specific file, choosing a model from the\n   dropdown, or picking a session are all intents.\n2. **Does it survive the next boundary?** If the answer dies on resume/reload/restart, it was\n   honoured but not recorded, and the setting will quietly win next time. Persist it beside the thing\n   it belongs to — session choices next to the session, not in global config.\n3. **Scope it to what was actually expressed.** An intent binds only the thing the gesture was about.\n   \"New Tab on `foo.ts`\" means *this file, this tab*; it does **not** mean \"start including active\n   files everywhere.\" A gesture is never a licence to overwrite the user's settings.\n\nKnown instances, kept here because each was found separately and only afterwards recognised as the\nsame bug:\n\n| Gesture | Default that overrides it | Status |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Switch model mid-session | `copilotCLI.model` reasserts on resume | `planning/backlog/session-model-persistence.md` |\n| *New Tab* on a specific file | `copilotCLI.includeActiveFile` | decided in v3.13.0: the click seeds that file regardless |\n| Switch to a specific session | `getMostRecentSession` picks by mtime, so a deliberate switch with no message sent is forgotten | unfiled |\n\n## Critical: Webview Build System\n\nesbuild.js manually copies each webview file to `dist/`. When adding a new directory under `src/webview/app/`, you MUST update `esbuild.js` with:\n1. A dist directory variable\n2. An `mkdirSync()` call\n3. A `copyFileSync()` call for each file\n\nWithout this, the webview silently fails (blank sidebar, no 'ready' message, no errors).\n\n## Component Hierarchy (Do Not Violate)\n\nMessageDisplay is a parent component that internally creates ToolExecution children. Never instantiate ToolExecution directly from main.js.\n\n**The guard is `tests/unit/components/MessageDisplay-tool-ownership.test.js`**, which mounts the\ncomponents and asserts the tool chip lands inside MessageDisplay's container. It replaced\n`main-full-integration.test.js`, whose eleven tests grepped `main.js` for `new MessageDisplay(` and\nfor the *absence* of `getElementById('messages')` — string matches that would have passed against a\ncomment, from a migration that finished long ago. Every component it named has behavioural coverage\nunder `tests/unit/components/`.\n\nThe hierarchy:\n\n```\nmain.js → SessionToolbar, MessageDisplay, AcceptanceControls, InputArea\nMessageDisplay → ToolExecution (internal child)\nInputArea → ActiveFileDisplay, StatusBar, PlanModeControls, SlashCommandPanel\n```\n\n## File Naming & Organization\n\n**A name must convey its value from a directory listing alone.** If you have to open the file to learn what it holds or which variant it is, the name has failed. For a contract with implementations, the contract takes the bare name and each implementation is named for what it implements:\n\n```\nhostBridge.ts        → the HostBridge interface\nvscodeHostBridge.ts  → the VS Code implementation\nacpHostBridge.ts     → the ACP implementation\n```\n\n**Multiple classes in one file require a stated reason.** The default is one class per file, named for the class. Co-location is a decision to defend — shared private state, a contract and its no-op default, a sealed variant set — not a convenience to fall into. Write the reason in the file header, and tie it to the choice it justifies rather than only describing the mechanism.\n\nBoth rules exist because `hostBridge.ts` shipped holding an interface, a factory, and a class under a generic name. Months later it cost a full session to answer \"is there even an interface?\" — the answer was yes, invisibly. See `planning/backlog/hostbridge-split-and-fallback-seam.md`.\n\nCaveat: legibility alone rarely justifies renaming existing code. A rename that leaves the underlying coupling in place is cosmetic — pair it with a structural fix, or leave it and document why.\n\n## Testing Approach\n\nThis project uses strict TDD. Tests must import production code, not mocks. A test that passes immediately without failing first is not valid.\n\n- Server-side tests (`tests/unit/extension/`) require `npm run compile-tests` first (compiles to `out/`).\n- Webview tests use JSDOM (`tests/helpers/jsdom-setup.js`, `jsdom-component-setup.js`).\n- Test helpers: `createTestDOM()`, `cleanupTestDOM()`, `createMockRpc()`, `createComponentDOM()`.\n- E2E tests (`tests/e2e/`) need a live Copilot SDK connection and compiled output.\n\n### Tests Must Test Active Functional Behavior\n\nTests must assert **live, functional behavior** — function calls, DOM state changes, emitted events, RPC calls. Tests that assert the presence of string literals, import statements, or commented-out code are not testing anything real.\n\n**When removing or changing code breaks a test, evaluate the test before restoring the code:**\n\n1. Was the test verifying real behavior that still matters? → **Fix the test** to cover the new implementation.\n2. Was the test verifying behavior that was intentionally removed? → **Delete the test.**\n3. Was the test matching against a string, comment, or dead import? → **Delete the test.** It was never verifying anything.\n\n**Never restore dead code just to make a test pass.** Example of this failure: a test asserting `src.includes('new StatusBar(')` was passing because that string appeared inside a `//` comment — the component had already been removed. The right fix was to delete both the dead code and the test.\n\n## SDK-First Development\n\nThe SDK source code lives at `research/copilot-sdk/*`. Before implementing any feature that touches the Copilot SDK (`sdkSessionManager.ts`, session lifecycle, model switching, tool registration, etc.):\n\n1. **Read the SDK source first.** Check `research/copilot-sdk/nodejs/src/` for the proper API — types, RPC methods, session events. The SDK often has purpose-built methods for what you need (e.g., `session.rpc.model.switchTo()` instead of destroy/resume).\n2. **Spike it.** Write a minimal script in `planning/spikes/<topic>/` that calls the SDK directly (no extension, no webview) to prove the behavior. See existing spikes for the pattern.\n3. **Then implement.** Use what the spike proves, not assumptions about how the SDK works.\n\nKey SDK reference files:\n\n- `research/copilot-sdk/nodejs/src/client.ts` — CopilotClient (createSession, resumeSession, listModels)\n- `research/copilot-sdk/nodejs/src/session.ts` — CopilotSession (sendAndWait, destroy, rpc accessor)\n- `research/copilot-sdk/nodejs/src/generated/rpc.ts` — All RPC methods (session.model.switchTo, session.mode.get, etc.)\n- `research/copilot-sdk/nodejs/src/generated/session-events.ts` — All session events (session.model_change, assistant.usage, etc.)\n- `research/copilot-sdk/nodejs/src/types.ts` — SessionConfig, ResumeSessionConfig, ModelInfo\n\n## Custom Tool Registration\n\nCustom tools in plan mode must be registered in TWO places in sdkSessionManager.ts:\n1. In `getCustomTools()` (the implementation)\n2. In the `availableTools` array (the SDK whitelist)\n\n## Session Files\n\nSessions stored at `~/.copilot/session-state/<session-id>/` containing `events.jsonl`, `plan.md`, `workspace.yaml`.\n\n## Copilot CLI Bundle (Lazy Install)\n\nThe extension does NOT trust the user's global `copilot` install. SDK ↔ CLI protocol changes between versions; SDK 0.3.0 declares `peerDependencies: { \"@github/copilot\": \"^1.0.36-0\" }`, and the user's global launcher is typically far behind (e.g. 1.0.5).\n\n`CliBundleService` resolves the CLI in this order:\n1. **local** — `node_modules/@github/copilot` (dev / F5).\n2. **managed** — `<globalStorageUri>/cli/<peer-range>/node_modules/@github/copilot`.\n3. **system** — `which copilot` (last resort, surfaces a warning if it doesn't satisfy the SDK peer-dep).\n\nIf none satisfy, it lazy-installs into the managed location via `npm install --prefix <dest> @github/copilot@<peer-range>`. Result is fed to `SDKSessionManager` as the `cliPath`. `CliCapabilityService` exposes feature flags from the resolved version (e.g. `supportsMcpListRpc`).\n\n</custom_instruction>\n<system_notifications>\nYou may receive messages wrapped in <system_notification> tags. These are automated status updates from the runtime (e.g., background task completions, shell command exits).\n\nWhen you receive a system notification:\n- Acknowledge briefly if relevant to your current work (e.g., \"Shell completed, reading output\")\n- Do NOT repeat the notification content back to the user verbatim\n- Do NOT explain what system notifications are\n- Continue with your current task, incorporating the new information\n- If idle when a notification arrives, take appropriate action (e.g., read completed agent results)\n\nNever generate your own system notifications or output text that includes <system_notification> tags. System notifications will be provided to you.\n</system_notifications>\n\n\n<exploration_and_reading_files>\nFiles are truncated at 20KB. Always use view_range for targeted reads on large files.\n- **Do all view calls in the same response.** Issue all independent view calls together (sections of same file or different files) — they run in parallel.\n- **Sequential only when necessary.** Only read one-at-a-time if you genuinely cannot know the next file without seeing the previous result.\n</exploration_and_reading_files>\n\n\n<session_context>\nSession folder: /home/smolen/.copilot/session-state/4dd65a29-62a8-4d7b-8383-af5eaae1d6a9\nPlan file: /home/smolen/.copilot/session-state/4dd65a29-62a8-4d7b-8383-af5eaae1d6a9/plan.md  (not yet created)\n\nContents:\n- files/: Persistent storage for session artifacts\n\nCreate a plan.md for tasks that require work across multiple phases or files. Write it once you have an overview of the work and update at large milestones. This helps you stay organized and lets the user follow your progress.\nYou can skip writing a plan for straightforward tasks\n\nfiles/ persists across checkpoints for artifacts that shouldn't be committed (e.g., architecture diagrams, task breakdowns, user preferences).\n</session_context>\nYour goal is to deliver complete, working solutions. If your first approach doesn't fully solve the problem, iterate with alternative approaches. Don't settle for partial fixes. Verify your changes actually work before considering the task done.\n\n<task_completion>\n* A task is not complete until the expected outcome is verified and persistent\n* After configuration changes (e.g., package.json, requirements.txt), run the necessary commands to apply them (e.g., `npm install`, `pip install -r requirements.txt`)\n* After starting a background process, verify it is running and responsive (e.g., test with `curl`, check process status)\n* If an initial approach fails, try alternative tools or methods before concluding the task is impossible\n</task_completion>\nRespond concisely to the user, but be thorough in your work."}

## Post-Mortem Review — 2026-08-23

**Reviewed by:** Copilot CLI (Claude Sonnet 4.6)

### Bug Found in This Log

**Tab tools not rendering** — session `474592bb` ran 4 tool calls (bash ×1, view ×3) that
executed successfully on the CLI side but produced no tool chips in the tab UI.

### Root Cause

`wireManagerEvents` in `extension.ts` calls `host.attachManager(manager)` first, then registers
~9 window-scoped handlers via `host.ownManagerSubscription(...)`. When a tab's `ensureStarted()`
resolved, it called `host.attachManager(manager)` a second time with the same manager instance.

The old `attachManager` implementation treated any call as a replacement: it called
`releaseWindowSubscriptions()`, which disposed every subscription `wireManagerEvents` had just
registered, then re-added only the host-level routing. The window-scoped pipeline — status bar,
sub-agent dock, MCP state, dropdown refresh, `[CLI Status]` — was silently dead for the entire
session.

**Signature in this log:**

Sidebar tools (session `4dd65a29`) produce two `[Tool Start]` lines per call:
```
[INFO] [Tool Start] tool=bash mode=work session=4dd65a29   ← SDKSessionManager
[INFO] [Tool Start] bash                                    ← extension.ts window handler
```

Tab tools (session `474592bb`) produce only one:
```
[INFO] [Tool Start] tool=bash mode=work session=474592bb   ← SDKSessionManager
                                                            ← window handler MISSING
```

This log was captured at **14:04–14:09 CDT**. The fix landed in commit `6b3d65c` at **15:09 CDT**
the same day, 65 minutes later. This log is the evidence the commit message cites.

### Fix

Idempotence guard at the top of `ChatSessionHost.attachManager`:

```typescript
if (this.#manager === manager) {
    return;
}
```

Object-identity (`===`) is correct: the same instance is a no-op; a different instance from a
restart or session switch is a real replacement and still goes through the full replace path.

### Fix Verification (2026-08-23)

Five tests in `tests/unit/extension/chat-session-host-manager-lifetime.test.js` cover the failure
modes introduced by the guard:

| Test | What it proves |
| --- | --- |
| keeps the window subscriptions the composition root registered | Core bug: `ownManagerSubscription` entries survive a second attach |
| does not tear down and rebuild its own routing either | No double-subscription — one event fires one chip |
| still routes after the second attach | Surface still receives events |
| does not dispose the manager it is being handed again | Idempotence does not kill the active manager |
| a genuinely different manager still replaces the old one | Real replacements (restarts, session switches) still work |

All 14 tests in that file pass. Fix confirmed correct.
